markdown:
Good observation, and here's exactly what's happening: server restarts recover the *conversation* (SDK `resume` + the event log) but not the *in-flight turn* — the generation that was running dies with the old process, and the new one boots with status `idle`, waiting for input. Nothing re-delivers a "continue," so you've been supplying it by hand.

Three ways to handle it, and my recommendation is the second:

1. **Keep as is** — restart = deliberate pause point. Safe, but in dev mode every server-file edit restarts tsx, so you end up nudging constantly (you just lived this).
2. **Auto-resume with guardrails** — on boot, if the log shows the last turn never completed (working status at death, no `turn_complete`), auto-enqueue a synthetic "server restarted mid-turn — pick up where the transcript leaves off." Guardrails: at most once per boot, skipped if you already have messages waiting (those deliver first and provide direction), and it renders visibly in the conversation so it's never silent. This matches the auto-mode philosophy — restarts are supposed to be survivable plumbing, not stop signs.
3. **One-click resume** — no auto-behavior; the work bar shows "resumed after restart — last turn cut short" with a *pick up where you left off* button. You stay in control, one click instead of typing.

One piece already improved this turn: queued-but-undelivered messages now persist and auto-deliver FIFO on boot, so *those* no longer need a nudge. # Review — wave 1 (2026-08-18, first hands-on session)

Source: the user's first real test of the walking skeleton, with screenshots.
Protocol: triage every item — accept into a task (note it), fix directly (check off
with the commit sha), or push back with reasons (never silently drop). The user
verifies checked items.

- [ ] R1 — Tasks panel: items must be clickable to expand — full detail, edit
  subject/status from the UI, and (per SCOPE.md) show what the dispatch prompt to a
  subagent would look like, editable.
  Accepted → Task #11 (editing needs a wire-protocol addition; dispatch preview
  rides on the canUseTool spike). Partial in 9e2e1af: delegated badges link tasks
  to live dispatches.
- [x] R2 — Git timeline: commits must be clickable to expand — full commit message,
  per-file diffstat, and the jump-to-conversation link made obvious.
  Refined (user): keep v1 simple — an expand view fed by GET /api/commit?sha=
  (git show --stat --patch; endpoint exists). Pinned for later: deep-link each
  commit to GitHub's diff view once push/remote awareness exists.
  Fixed in 887d721 — expandable card: full message + stat, collapsible patch,
  explicit ↷ jump-to-conversation link.
- [x] R3 — Right rail: must be expandable/resizable (the goal doc is cramped at a
  fixed 290px); ideally the goal document (SCOPE.md) is editable in place — edit →
  save to file → agent notified it changed.
  Resize fixed in 887d721 (drag handle, 240–720px, width persisted).
  Edit-in-place accepted → Task #12.
- [x] R4 — New first-class noun, the Review: an affordance for batch feedback from a
  testing wave. Items with optional screenshots/quotes, each tracked
  open → accepted(task) → addressed(commit) → verified, or declined(reasons).
  Stored as files in .clyde/reviews/ (this file is the v0), rendered as a panel with
  burn-down, items thread-anchorable. Add to SCOPE.md and the standing orders
  (triage every item, check off with commit links).
  v0 fixed in 887d721 (reviews tab + burn-down, SCOPE.md §8) and 9e2e1af (standing
  orders). Superseded in part by the lifecycle-test decision: Review stays a lens;
  folding items into Tasks with provenance → Task #13.
- [x] R5 — New-session affordance: a "New session" action in the UI, and persist the
  unsent queue across server restarts. (Today: boot once with --new; in dev mode the
  flag sticks across tsx restarts, which is a footgun.)
  Update: queue persistence is done, and non-urgent messages now steer mid-turn by
  default so the queue rarely holds anything — remaining: the New-session UI action.
  FIFO boot-drain + strict ordering fixed in 9e2e1af; auto-resume of cut-short
  turns added on top (user chose option 2). New-session UI action → Task #14.
- [x] R6 — Sidebar replies misattributed: the positional first-message heuristic
  tagged a main-flow sentence into a thread. Addressed server-side with declared
  attribution — per-thread [[sidebar:<id>]] markers, multi-message and
  multiple-threads-in-flight safe. Verified this session across three concurrent
  sidebar threads.
- [x] R7 — Logs view: the server now writes structured JSONL to
  .clyde/logs/server.jsonl and serves GET /api/logs?tail=N. Build a UI tab that
  renders it — and read the file yourself when debugging Clyde.
  Fixed in 887d721 — logs tab with level styling, debug toggle, 5s refresh.
- [x] R8 — Agents view: subagents are now first-class (delegation is in your
  standing orders), so give them a tab: each dispatch as a card — agent type,
  description, prompt (expandable), status (running until its tool_result arrives),
  duration, live tool-call count via parentToolUseId. Link to tasks by convention:
  when delegating a task-list item, put its exact subject in the Task description
  and mark it in_progress; Tasks panel shows a "delegated" badge. Implementation
  note: observeToolCall in agentSession.ts mints a random toolUseId for dispatch
  events — pass the real tool_use block id through so dispatch ↔ result ↔ subagent
  activity correlate.
  Fixed in 9e2e1af — agents tab cards (status/duration/tool counts), real-id
  correlation, delegated badges.
- [ ] R10 — Plumb the REAL AskUserQuestion tool (supersedes any ask_user sibling
  idea; the user loves this tool). Verified SDK contract: available by default in
  headless sessions (don't exclude it if a tools array is ever set); under
  bypassPermissions the canUseTool callback is skipped unless AskUserQuestion has an
  explicit "ask" permission rule (or use a PreToolUse hook) — add that. On
  interception: render the questions as an option card in the conversation UI
  (1–4 questions, 2–4 options each, header ≤12 chars, multiSelect, plus an "Other"
  free-text choice), set toolConfig.askUserQuestion.previewFormat: "html" to get
  rich option previews, and return {behavior: "allow", updatedInput: {questions,
  answers}} with answers keyed by exact question text (arrays for multiSelect).
  The callback may be held open indefinitely (documented, no timeout) — that's
  blocking mode for load-bearing forks. Non-blocking experiment: resolve
  immediately with a "posted — user will answer asynchronously; continue non-gated
  work" answer and steer the real click in later. Note: unavailable in subagents —
  asking is the primary agent's job. Standing orders addition: ask early and often —
  before ambiguous or taste-dependent work, put 2–4 concrete options with a
  recommendation; distill answers into DECISIONS.md and/or tasks.
  Accepted → Task #15.
- [x] R9 — Mid-turn responsiveness discipline: user messages arrive mid-turn as
  queued_command attachments and you see them (verified in the transcript), but you
  file them as tasks without answering — the user experiences silence. Update your
  standing orders (CLYDE_PROTOCOL in agentSession.ts): respond to mid-turn user
  messages in your very next message — sidebar comments FIRST, with their exact
  [[sidebar:<id>]] token — a brief direct answer, then continue working; filing a
  task is in addition to replying, never instead of it. Also prefer ending turns at
  logical checkpoints rather than marathon turns. (Your Task #8 FIFO fix covers the
  queue-jumping half of this.)
  Fixed in 9e2e1af — standing orders updated (mid-turn answers + checkpoint
  discipline + delegation/task linking), FIFO half in the same commit; practiced
  through the rest of this session.
